# Candidate sensor technologies
- Sensor-T2: thin-pitch sensor with large signal sharing.
- Sensor-T3: planar sensor, standard pitch.
- Sensor-T1: 3D-electrode sensor, larger pitch.
All are qualified for bump bonding to the readout chip.

# Irradiation and test-beam campaign, 2026
Sensors were irradiated with reactor neutrons to 2e16 neq/cm^2 and measured at the SPS test beam.
Hit efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2:
- Sensor-T2: 82.0% (strong charge trapping; full depletion no longer reachable at the maximum bias)
- Sensor-T3: 98.5%
- Sensor-T1: 99.2%
Requirement for the innermost layer: >= 97% up to end of life.

# Meeting notes 2026-03-02
Cooling: CO2 evaporative cooling at -35 C confirmed. Mechanics: the carbon-fibre staves are on schedule.

# Earlier simulation summary (2025, 150 um, unirradiated)
Single-hit resolution: Sensor-T2 6.0 um, Sensor-T3 9.0 um, Sensor-T1 14.0 um.

# Readout chip
The common readout chip supports 50x50 um^2 pixels and a 1.5 GHz/cm^2 hit rate. All candidates are compatible.

# Services
The power budget per module is 7 W. Serial powering is the baseline.

# Schedule
Sensor market survey closes in Q2; pre-production in Q4.

content.text: Sensor-T2 fails the end-of-life requirement (82% efficiency against ≥97%), so it's out. T1 and T3 both pass. I'll check how resolution depends on thickness for those two.
Sensor-T3 is best near 100 µm, and the 2025 summary gave about 9.0 µm at 150 µm. I'll check 150 µm directly before deciding.

input.justification: Sensor-T2 is excluded: after 2e16 neq/cm^2 its hit efficiency is 82.0%, far below the >=97% end-of-life requirement, due to strong charge trapping. Of the two remaining radiation-tolerant options, Sensor-T3 (planar) gives better unirradiated single-hit resolution than Sensor-T1 (3D) at every thickness simulated. Simulated T3 resolution: 10.0 um at 50 um, 9.4 um at 100 um, 8.9 um at 150 um, 9.5 um at 200 um. Sensor-T1 ranged from 14.1 to 16.2 um. 150 um gave the best T3 resolution among the points tested, and it is within the 50-300 um range. Sensor-T3 measured 98.5% efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm^2, meeting the requirement. Caveat: the irradiation result is not tied to a specific thickness in the document, and the resolutions are unirradiated, so post-irradiation resolution at 150 um was not simulated.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be one of the three candidate technologies
Suitable for innermost-layer radiation environment (>=97% hit efficiency at end of life, 2e16 neq/cm^2)

Simulated unirradiated resolution: T3 8.93 um at 150 um, the best of the points tested (T3 9.4 um at 100 um, 9.5 um at 200 um, 10.0 um at 50 um). Sensor-T1 14.1-16.2 um; Sensor-T2 6.0 um at 150 um (2025 summary) but fails the radiation requirement.
